transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card customer support. My name is Marcus. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Hello Marcus, my name is Lena Mortimer.
Agent: Thank you, Ms. Mortimer. For security, could you verify the last four digits of your card and your billing zip code?
Customer: Sure, the last four digits are 8821, and the zip code is 97204.
Agent: Thank you, that matches our records. What can I help you with today?
Customer: Well, I was looking over my statement that came out back on October 6th, about nine days ago, and there is an issue with a charge from Northfold Outfitters.
Agent: I can certainly look into that with you. What was the date of the transaction and the total amount?
Customer: The charge went through on September 26th for $148.99.
Agent: I have that charge from Northfold Outfitters on September 26th for $148.99 right here. Could you describe what happened with the purchase?
Customer: I ordered a winter coat on their website in a size medium. When the package finally arrived, they had sent me an extra-large coat in an entirely different style.
Agent: Did the package include a receipt or packing slip showing what was supposed to be in the order?
Customer: Yes, the invoice inside listed the medium coat that I originally ordered, but the actual garment in the box was the wrong style and an extra-large.
Agent: Have you contacted Northfold Outfitters regarding the incorrect item?
Customer: I sent customer support an email a few days ago with photos of the coat and the tag, but I haven't heard back from them yet.
Agent: Do you currently still have the item that was delivered?
Customer: Yes, it is right here in the original box with all the tags on it.
Agent: So to recap the details so far, you placed an order with Northfold Outfitters on September 26th for $148.99, which showed on your October 6th statement, you ordered a medium winter coat, but received an extra-large coat in a completely different style, and you currently still have that package.
